The duty a body needs

Count feet and you get a number with no simulation in it. A polygon needs three corners, so β ≥ 3/N for any gait at all. A wave lifts a whole flank in turn, so it needs more feet down than one flank has legs: β ≥ ½ + 1/N. An alternating gait splits the legs in two, so it needs β ≥ ½ — and on six legs that is 3/N, which is why the insect tripod cannot be beaten.

Press measure it: the page walks this exact beast a full settled cycle at each of 60 duty factors and asks, 480 times per cycle, whether the plumb line falls inside the polygon. The dashed line is the prediction. Nothing is fitted.
